Text Field #1:
Devops is a combination of development and operations that provides ongoing value through the combination of people processes, and technology

Teams that move to Devops build better products faster and deliver higher customer satisfaction than traditional teams

[b]This game is designed[/b] to playfully teach trade-offs and learn Devops From all perspectives.
The game further aims to create team spirit by providing opportunities to help each other and have disccusions
Text Field #2: Anyone with any degree of experience working in DevOps teams. The combination of people with different levels of experience is ideal.
Text Field #4:
- Rules
 - Game board
 - 16 pawns in 8 colors, 2 per color
 - dice
 - 26 action cards
 - 171 question cards
- 171 answer cards
- list of answers and some notes for the facilitator
- hourglass
Text Field #5:
-Place the game board on the table

 - sort the question cards per color and put them in number order. Insert 3 to 4 action cards randomly into each pile. Place the piles lengthwise on the game board in order of the phase on the game board.

- There is a division between Basic Cards and Professional Cards. the question cards for the more experienced players can be used if more experienced players are participating, but you can also leave them out.
Text Field #6:
-If there is no facilitator, sort the answer cards. Make a pile of each color and put the cards in the right order. Place the piles next to the game board next to the question cards. If there is a facilitator, this step is not necessary, the list of answers can then be used.

 -prefereably, form teams of 2, however the game can be played by individual player or teams of 3. each team chooses 2 pawns of the same color, but do not place them on the game board yet

Text Field #1:
The game board has 16 squares.

Each color has a stack of cards: Plan,Code,Build,Test,Release,Deploy, Operate,Monitor.
Each player starts on the first square of phase plan (if they get to play a pawn).
Text Field #2:
Choose a player to start and flip the hourglass. This player Rolls the dice and moves their pawn the numbers indicated on the dice. The first step is to place the pawn on the game board. More than one pawn may be on 1 square at a time.
Take a card from the pile belonging to the square you end up on and read it out loud.

Afterwards, in clockwise order, it is the next player's turn.
Text Field #3:
If you get the answer right. Then you can stay at your new spot. 
if you got the answer wrong, you return to where you were initially standing.

The answered card will then be placed on the discard pile.
Text Field #4:
Did you draw an action card? Then the action on the card applies.
Each question card comes with an answer card. This may be turned over by one of the other players after answering the question. If facilitator is present, the answer cards are not needed.
Text Field #5:
There are 3 types of questions: 
Open Ended questions - has an answer card with a suggestion. The group decides if you answered correctly.
Statement - explains if and how you apply this. If the group agrees with your answer, you move forward.
Multiple choice questions - if you answer correctly, you may move forward.
Text Field #6:
Events in the game can cause you to have multiple pawns in play. If you have multiple pawns running, after rolling the dice you may choose which one to move forward.
 - When your first pawn crosses the finish square (you don't have to finish exactly on it) answer the question. if you answered the question wrong, go back. If you answered the question correctly, This pawn has finished, and you may place this pawn on the finish space
- Then you continue playing with your second pawn.

Text Field #1: This game has been developed to playfully learn to make trade-offs and to get to know DevOps from all perspectives. The game is further intended to develop team spirit by providing an opportunity to help each other and have open discussions.
Text Field #2: The game can be played by a DevOps team, in which the scrum master himself also plays. The scrum master is therefore the game leader. The game can also be played by a DevOps team, where playing the game is faciltated by a third party.
Text Field #3: The game leader should instigate team spirit as much as possible by encouraging participants to work together to answer questions. The participant who is asked a question should be encouraged to answer on their own, however if they are unable to figure it out, the game leader should challenge the other participants to help.
Text Field #4: Discussions among participants about (answering) a question often also provide great insight into, among other things, the functioning of the team and where improvements can be made. Record these improvement opportunities, so that they can be included in a retrospective.
Text Field #5:
Read the rules carefully and explain them to the players. The rules of the game indicate how the game should be set up. Everyone can play for themselves up to 8 participants.
If there are more than 8 participants, the game master divides the particpants into teams of two. You can also choose to form teams of two participants with fewer than eight participants. When composing the teams, consider the experience of the participants.

Text Field #2: and can use any color that you want
Text Field #3: Express to the participants that playing the game is meant to be fun as well. To encourage participation, you could also use treatments (e.g. candies).
